# Tasks device notifications

## Enable on your Android phone or desktop
Open Tasks → Run and tap **Test notification**. On first use it asks for notification permission, connects this device, and sends a real server push. Check your actual device notification tray. You can also use **Enable notifications** to connect without sending a test. In a task's Edit dialog, choose **Remind me**, a future date/time, and Save. A due date alone does not create a timed reminder. The reminders panel reports how many are synced to this device.

Notifications use Web Push and a Cloudflare Durable Object alarm, so the Tasks tab does not have to stay open. You do not need your Mac browser server for task reminders. Each device must enable notifications separately. On iPhone/iPad, use a supported OS/browser and add Tasks to the Home Screen before enabling. Android Chrome can receive them through the device notification system. Browser permission, OS notification/battery/network settings, private/incognito mode, device availability, browser support and push-service availability affect delivery and timing. This is not a guaranteed alarm clock.

Push messages intentionally contain no task titles or notes. The service worker reads a device-local IndexedDB mirror to show the task name and its due date, when set. If several reminders are due together, one notification lists up to three task names/dates and summarizes the remainder. If local details are unavailable, it shows a generic reminder instead. Clicking it opens the private Tasks app and may require signing in again. Task titles/due dates are mirrored into IndexedDB on this device so the background worker can read them while Tasks is closed. They are never sent to the reminder server or push provider. Task records remain browser-local; only reminder IDs/timestamps, a device ID and the push endpoint are stored on the server. This is notification scheduling, not task synchronization across devices. To see the same tasks on another device, export/import tasks, then enable reminders on that device.

Complete/delete a task, remove its reminder, or disable notifications to cancel its device's server schedule. These changes must sync while online; if a cancellation cannot sync, the previous scheduled notification may still arrive. Disable on each device separately. Re-enabling preserves the browser's permission setting. Permission can also be revoked in browser/OS settings. Expired subscriptions are removed after a push service rejects them. Sending to a push service is not proof that the device displayed the message.

## Server implementation
`TaskPush` is a SQLite-backed Durable Object, configured in wrangler.jsonc. Cloudflare's Git deployment creates its binding/migration. It generates and stores its VAPID keypair inside Durable Object storage; there are no API keys or private VAPID keys to paste into the browser or commit to Git. The gateway is protected by the existing owner-only Access check, and same-origin JSON is required for mutations. The service worker has no fetch handler and does not cache or bypass the hub login.

The scheduler sends standard payload-free Web Push POSTs with ES256 VAPID authentication (RFC 8292). The browser's push endpoint is restricted to known browser push services. Signed tokens are reused for six hours and expire within twelve. At most twelve devices and five hundred reminders per device are stored; each device is a separate storage record. One push aggregates simultaneously due reminders, with a stable notification tag. Transient errors retry up to three attempts; permanent 404/410 endpoints are removed. Alarms are at-least-once; the server records accepted attempts to avoid repeat scheduling, but crashes or delayed providers may still cause duplicates. Generic notification tagging coalesces them.

Cloudflare storage/alarms and browser push quotas apply. If deployment cannot create the Durable Object namespace, the UI reports that notification storage is not configured. Do not work around an error by granting public access to the API.

Tests cover signatures, scheduling/deduplication, cancellations, retry/expiration and authentication. Automated browser tests mock notification permission and push subscription; actual phone delivery must be checked with **Test notification** on your device.

## Android Chrome verification and recovery
1. Open the live Tasks Run page in a normal Chrome tab, sign in, and tap **Enable notifications**. Choose **Allow** for this site. Android Settings → Apps → Chrome → Notifications must also be enabled.
2. Tap **Test notification** and check the Android notification tray. The status “Sent to your push service” confirms provider acceptance, not a displayed notification.
3. Give an unfinished task a **Remind me** time a couple of minutes ahead and Save. Wait until the panel reports the reminder is scheduled, then leave Tasks or lock the phone. You do not need to leave the Tasks tab open, but force-stopping Chrome or OS restrictions can prevent delivery.

Due reminders and tests use high Web Push urgency to improve delivery while Android is idle; this remains subject to browser/OS/provider limits. If a push subscription expires, Enable notifications becomes available again and the expired browser subscription is removed. If the server's application key changes, Enable replaces a subscription tied to the old key. Setup has a timeout rather than leaving the permission button stuck indefinitely. Blocking site permission or Chrome's Android notification permission must be corrected on the phone.

Verification now also includes a real Chromium service worker processing a simulated payload-free push with no Tasks page open and creating a notification with the correct destination. This confirms the browser handler, not real FCM-to-phone delivery; that final check is the device's Test notification above.

## Cloudflare sender compatibility
The push sender binds native `fetch` to the Worker global and uses `redirect: 'manual'`; Cloudflare's runtime rejects an unbound method call and does not implement `redirect: 'error'`. Redirect responses are treated as failures and never followed, preserving the push-provider allowlist boundary. This was verified by executing a real signed outbound POST from the Durable Object in workerd, rather than only mocking fetch.

Send/signing/time-out exceptions now produce their own error codes (`push_send_failed`, `push_signing_failed`, `push_timeout`). They are no longer mislabeled as a provider HTTP 503. A real HTTP response from the push provider retains its status in the displayed error. Tests guard both runtime compatibility choices and the distinction between local send failures and actual provider errors.

## Reminder display details
Refresh Tasks once after this update so its background worker updates and the local reminder details are saved. Existing enabled devices reconnect without re-enrolling. Reminder edits update the local mirror; completing/deleting tasks removes them. Disabling notifications clears that device's reminder mirror. Shown reminders are tracked by task ID and reminder timestamp to avoid using an old task title on later test pushes; changing the reminder time makes it eligible again. Due dates are calendar dates formatted locally without a UTC day shift. Task names/dates may appear on the lock screen according to the device's notification settings. Test pushes with no due tasks continue to use the generic notification.

## Recurrence
Recurring reminders additionally sync the selected frequency and IANA time zone; task titles, due dates, notes and checklists stay on the device. The Durable Object persists a next-occurrence cursor and advances it after delivery without needing the page open. Re-syncing the same rule retains the cursor. After repeated delivery failures, the current occurrence is skipped and future recurring reminders are retained. Completing/deleting a task removes its server schedule after syncing. Reopening resumes future occurrences. Daily, weekday, weekly and monthly rules follow the saved time zone, including daylight saving and month-end clamping. Local notification deduplication tracks each occurrence, rather than marking a repeating task permanently shown after its first reminder.
